title: People central to the method
blurb: Explain how the principles, practices and processes depend on people, and how each principle is applied through the people element.
question: A project manager gradually lets a trusted team manager make more decisions as the team's skills grow. Which principle is the people element applying?

teach.h: Why people sit at the centre
teach.body: People is one of PRINCE2 7's five integrated elements, alongside principles, practices, processes and the project context. A project exists to deliver change, and that change affects people's everyday routines and responsibilities. How well it lands depends on the team's capabilities, the strength of their relationships and the people impacted. In plain English: the method is a recipe book, and only people can cook with it.

teach.caption: The four parts of the people element shown in the official figure (manual fig 3.3).

teach.body: PRINCE2 explains how each principle plays out in the people element. Learning, delegation, stage reviews and product design all succeed or fail on relationships, trust and behaviour. Foundation questions often describe a people action and ask which principle it applies, so learn the signature of each one in the table that follows.

teach.h: How each principle applies to people
head: Principle
Applied to people as
rows: Sharing hidden knowledge through social learning
Deciding at the most local level that has the knowledge
Reviewing influencers and key relationships at stages
Co-creating products with business, user and supplier
Addressing people factors throughout the lifecycle
teach.caption: Paraphrased from manual 3.5.1.

teach.body: Learn from experience: behaviours, culture and relationships are hard to document, so they are best learned socially in a knowledge-sharing environment. Manage by exception: escalate when a decision could affect other areas; how far you delegate depends on confidence and trust, and changes as skills grow. Manage by stages: stages often mark a change in influencers. Focus on products: co-creation improves adoption, reduces handover risks and covers operational and maintenance needs.

rows.label: Key idea
values: Most local level with the knowledge

teach.h: People in the practices and processes
head: Where
People in action
rows: Roles fitted to people; relationships managed
PM co-creates each work package with the TM
Team performance, health and well-being reviewed
Safety, well-being and social cohesion of the team
teach.caption: From the role descriptions and the practices applied in each process.

teach.body: Ellerby Foods is installing a new packaging line. Project manager Nadia Rahman pairs new engineers with operators who ran the old line, so know-how passes on informally. As shift supervisor Kofi Mensah proves himself, she lets him decide more, escalating only what affects other lines. At each stage boundary she reviews who the key influencers now are. Operators and maintenance staff help write the product descriptions. Executive Alan Shaw asks about overtime and fatigue at every board meeting.

teach.h: Which principle is the people action applying?

teach.text: Do not mix up the two most confused links. Knowledge sharing and social learning apply learn from experience. Deciding at the most local level where the knowledge resides applies manage by exception, even though both involve people sharing what they know.

items: People is one of the five integrated elements; the principles, practices and processes are applied by people.
Learn from experience: hidden knowledge, social learning, a knowledge-sharing environment (manual 3.5.1).
Manage by exception: decide at the most local level with the knowledge; delegation depends on confidence and trust.
Manage by stages: stages mark changes in influencers and key relationships. Focus on products: co-creation improves adoption and cuts handover risk.
The board focuses on the team's safety and well-being and supports social cohesion.

summary: You can now explain why people sit at the centre of PRINCE2 7 and match a people action to the principle it applies. You can also show where people appear in the practices and processes, including the board's duty for the team's safety and well-being.

A.q: Which of these is one of PRINCE2 7's five integrated elements?
A.why: The five integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and the project context (manual 1.2).

whyNot.0: Tolerances are a control used under manage by exception, not an integrated element.
whyNot.1: Themes were a 6th edition element; PRINCE2 7 uses practices.
whyNot.2: Stakeholders are covered within the people element; they are not an element themselves.

A.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. In the people element, the [?] principle is applied by making decisions at the most local level where the knowledge to make and own them resides.
A.why: Deciding at the most local level where the knowledge resides is how the people element applies manage by exception (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience in the people element is about sharing hidden knowledge through social learning.
whyNot.2: Manage by stages in the people element is about stages marking changes in influencers and key relationships.
whyNot.3: Focus on products in the people element is about co-creating products with business, user and supplier communities.

A.q: How does the people element apply the learn from experience principle?
options: Sharing hidden knowledge through social learning
Deciding at the most local level that has the knowledge
Reviewing key relationships at each stage boundary
A.why: Much valuable knowledge is hidden in the project ecosystem, and people factors are best learned through social learning in a knowledge-sharing environment (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.1: Deciding at the most local level is how the people element applies manage by exception.
whyNot.2: Reviewing relationships at stage boundaries is how the people element applies manage by stages.
whyNot.3: Co-creating products is how the people element applies focus on products.

B.q:
Which two statements about people and the principles are correct?
1. Stages often mark a change in influencers and key relationships.
2. Behaviours and culture are easy to capture fully in the lessons log.
3. The extent of delegation depends on confidence and trust in key relationships.
4. Co-creating products tends to increase handover risks.
B.why: Stages often mark changes in influencers (1), and delegation depends on confidence and trust in key relationships (3) (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: people factors are hard to document and are best learned through social learning.
whyNot.1: Both are false: people factors are hard to document, and co-creation reduces handover risks.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: co-creating products reduces handover risks.

B.q: A project manager lets a trusted team manager make more decisions as the team's skills grow, escalating matters that could affect other areas. Which principle is the people element applying?
B.why: Deciding at the most local level, escalating when other areas could be affected, with delegation based on trust that adapts as skills grow, is manage by exception (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.1: Learn from experience in the people element concerns knowledge sharing and social learning.
whyNot.2: Manage by stages concerns stages as points to review relationships and decisions.
whyNot.3: Tailoring adapts the method to the project; delegating on the basis of trust is manage by exception.

B.q: Which project board responsibility in PRINCE2 7 relates directly to the team as people?
options: Focusing on the safety and well-being of the team
Producing highlight reports for the business layer
B.why: The project board's responsibilities include focusing on the safety and well-being of the project team.

whyNot.0: Project-level tolerances are set by the business layer, not the board.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports are produced by the project manager for the board.
whyNot.3: The project product description is prepared in starting up a project, not written by the board.

C.q: At a stage boundary, a project manager reviews who the key influencers now are and how the team works with the wider organization. Which principle is the people element applying, and why?
options: Learn from experience, because lessons are logged at the boundary
Manage by exception, because tolerances are reset for the next stage
Focus on products, because the next stage's products are defined
Manage by stages, because stages often mark changes in relationships
C.why: Stages often mark a change in influencers and key relationships, so they are good points to review how people interact (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Lessons may be reviewed at a boundary, but that does not explain reviewing key influencers and relationships.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set for the next stage, but that is not why relationships are reviewed.
whyNot.2: Products for the next stage are planned, but the action described is about people and relationships.

C.q: Operators and maintenance engineers help write the product descriptions for a new packaging line. Which principle is applied, and what does PRINCE2 say it achieves?
options: Learn from experience; it captures lessons for future projects
Manage by exception; it pushes decisions to the lowest level
Focus on products; it improves adoption and reduces handover risk
Define roles; it confirms who is accountable for each product
C.why: Co-creating products, with agreed product descriptions, applies focus on products and improves development and adoption while reducing handover risks (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience is about sharing knowledge; co-designing products applies focus on products.
whyNot.1: Manage by exception is about where decisions are made, not about co-designing products.
whyNot.3: Defining roles is about responsibilities and relationships; co-designing products applies focus on products.

C.q: Which statement best explains why PRINCE2 7 places people at the centre of the method?
options: The method is applied by people, and the change affects people
People replace the practices as the main element of PRINCE2 7
The people element is a separate stage run before initiation
People are managed through the issues practice in PRINCE2 7
C.why: The principles, practices and processes are applied by the people involved, and the change the project delivers affects people's routines and responsibilities (manual 1.2, chapter 3).

whyNot.1: People sit alongside principles, practices, processes and the project context; they do not replace the practices.
whyNot.2: The people element runs throughout the project; it is not a stage.
whyNot.3: The issues practice handles issues and changes to baselines, not people management.

reteach.title: A recipe book cannot cook
reteach.question: Why can two cooks with the same recipe book serve very different dinners?

blocks.body: The recipe book is the method: principles, practices and processes. What lands on the plate depends on the cooks: how they share tips (learn from experience), who decides on seasoning (manage by exception), when they pause to check the kitchen is working (manage by stages) and whether the diners helped choose the menu (focus on products). A head chef who ignores tired cooks will serve worse food.

blocks.text: Sharing tips is learning; letting the trusted cook decide is delegation. Keep learn from experience and manage by exception apart.

explain.body: The official figure for people central to the method has four parts: leading successful change, leading successful teams, communication, and people at the centre.

test.q: Which is one of the parts of the 'people central to the method' model?
test.why: The model's parts are leading successful change, leading successful teams, communication, and people at the centre (fig 3.3).

whyNot.0: Managing product delivery is a process.
whyNot.2: Manage by exception is a principle.
whyNot.3: Quality assurance is part of the quality practice.

explain.body: Behaviours, culture and relationships are hard to document, so they are best learned through social learning. That needs a collaborative environment that encourages knowledge sharing.

test.q: Why does PRINCE2 say people factors such as behaviours and culture are best learned through social learning?
options: They are recorded in the risk register
They are set by the business layer
test.why: People factors such as behaviours, culture and relationships are difficult to document (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: The risk register holds specific risks, not behaviours and culture.
whyNot.1: Culture emerges from people; it is not set by the business layer.
whyNot.2: Checkpoints are progress reports; that is not the reason given.

explain.body: Decisions should be made at the most local level where the knowledge resides and escalated when they could affect other areas. The extent of delegation depends on confidence and trust, and adapts as skills grow.

test.q: In the people element, what does the extent of delegation often depend on?
options: The number of management stages in the project plan
The size of the change budget
Confidence and trust in key relationships
test.why: The extent of delegation often depends on the confidence and trust in key relationships (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: The number of stages is a planning decision, not the basis for delegation.
whyNot.1: The change budget funds approved changes.
whyNot.3: Delegation in this sense is based on trust, not the executive's seniority.

explain.body: In PRINCE2 7 the board focuses on the team's safety and well-being, and the project manager and team managers monitor and support the safety and well-being of team members.

head: Role
Duty
rows: Focus on team safety and well-being

test.q: Which pair of roles both carry safety and well-being responsibilities in their PRINCE2 7 role descriptions?
test.why: Both the project manager and team manager role descriptions include monitoring and supporting the safety and well-being of team members.

whyNot.0: Neither project support nor project assurance holds this responsibility.
whyNot.2: The business layer is outside the project, and project support provides administrative services.
whyNot.3: Assurance checks performance independently; the business layer commissions the project.
